item.description:
PDFBoy 1.0 is here, with a whole new tool: Mark up.

Mark up (⇧⌘A)

  • Draw with a pen that follows your pressure. Sketch a rough line, arrow, box or circle and it turns into a clean shape.
  • Shapes: lines, arrows, boxes, ovals, speech bubbles, stars, a loupe and a mask.
  • Highlight, underline and strike through text. Add notes, text boxes and callouts. Quick stamps: ✓ ✕ ●, today’s date (also in the Buddhist era) and your initials.
  • Whiteout: cover a value in the paper’s own colour and type the new one in the same font.
  • Redact: black out text for real. When you save, it’s gone from the file, not just covered.
  • Select Area copies any part of a page as a picture.
  • “Your marks” in the corner lists everything you added.

Saving

  • Keep editable: your drawings, shapes, highlights and text stay changeable in Preview and other apps. Or flatten them into the page, as before.
  • Marks made in other apps can now be moved, restyled and deleted in PDFBoy.

Signing

  • Draw your signature with the trackpad, a mouse or a pen tablet, or sign on your iPhone or iPad.

Trial and licence

  • PDFBoy is free to try for 14 days. After that, opening, filling and marking up stay free, and a licence unlocks saving and exporting. Settings ▸ Licence.
• The pointing hand now shows over the toolbar’s zoom buttons, Save Copy and the other buttons, instead of an arrow.

A new look for the editor window

  • Tools on a shelf. View, Fill, Sign, Shrink, Combine & split and To Markdown now sit at the top of the sidebar (⌘1–⌘6). Fill shows how many blanks are left. Click “Tools” to fold the shelf down to the one you’re using.
  • Pages that show your progress. While filling, each page shows how many blanks are left, or a green tick when it’s done.
  • The boy has a seat. He sits on a card at the bottom of the sidebar: facts about the PDF when you’re reading, your progress and a tip while you fill, and a little celebration with Save Copy when everything is filled.
  • A calmer toolbar. Just the title, search (⌘F), zoom and one main button.
  • Hide the sidebar and the tools fold into a slim rail, with your progress as a ring around the boy.
  • Warmer colours throughout: a cream sidebar and a dotted desk behind the page, in Light and Dark Mode.

Also

  • PDFs now open for viewing; Fill is one click (or ⌘2) away.
  • Shrink tells you when a PDF can’t get meaningfully smaller, instead of offering a save that wouldn’t help.
